ask/ask: To learn, a classifier needs its scores to change so that its loss comes down. So for each score, two questions: which way should it move, and how much does the loss care?
ask/scores: Here are three options' scores, drawn as bars. Softmax turns them into probabilities, p: about zero point six, zero point three and zero point one.
ask/right: The right answer, y, is the middle option, option one. It got only zero point three.
ask/loss: The loss is minus the log of that: about one point two, this dot on the minus log curve. The less the right answer gets, the higher the dot climbs.
nudge/plain: Answer them the plain way: nudge one score a little, hold the others still, and watch the loss.
nudge/up0: Raise the first score, a wrong option's. Its share grows and the right answer's shrinks, so the dot climbs: the loss goes up.
nudge/slope0: A nudge of one hundredth raises the loss by six thousandths, which is zero point six times the nudge. That rate is the slope for the first score.
nudge/right1: Now raise the right answer's score. Its share grows, the dot slides down, and the loss falls by seven thousandths: a slope of minus zero point seven.
nudge/last2: Raise the last score, and the loss rises by only one thousandth: a slope of zero point one.
nudge/grad: One slope per score, each found with the others held still: these are the partial derivatives of the loss. Stacked into a vector, they make its gradient, partial L, partial s, called d s in code.
nudge/read: The sign says which way. Positive means raising that score raises the loss, so lower it; negative means raise it. The size says how much the loss cares.
why/compare: Set the slopes beside the probabilities. For the two wrong options they match exactly: zero point six and zero point six, zero point one and zero point one.
why/minus: The right answer's slope is its probability minus one: zero point three minus one is minus zero point seven.
why/why: Why? The same loss can be written as the log of the total, T, minus the right answer's score.
why/share: Raise any score a little, and T grows by e to that score, times the nudge, because e to the x is its own slope.
why/over: And the log's slope is one over T, so the log of T grows by that growth, divided by T: the option's probability, times the nudge.
why/one: The other part, minus the right score, moves only when the right score does, and by the whole nudge, the other way. That is the minus one.
onehot/collect: So every slope is that option's probability, and the right answer's loses one more. Collect what is taken away in a vector: a one at the right answer, zeros elsewhere.
onehot/name: It is called one-hot: exactly one entry is on, or hot, and the rest are off. Here it is zero, one, zero, written one-hot of y.
onehot/formula: So the gradient is p minus the one-hot vector: partial L, partial s, equals p minus one-hot of y.
onehot/sum: Its entries always add up to zero: p adds up to one, and the one-hot takes exactly one away. So the only negative entry is the right answer's.
onehot/step: To lower the loss, move the scores against the gradient: the right score goes up, and the wrong ones go down, the most probable wrong option the most.
onehot/done: As the right answer's probability nears one, every entry nears zero: there is little loss left to remove.
